raised.$description:
The resting lift of an element that sits above the page. Fixed across brands and viewports; only its colour moves, with the theme.

Used in:
Cards, tiles, chips — anything that sits above the page on color-surface.static.primary. Always pair it with color-border.static.secondary: the border is what keeps the element apart in dark mode and in high contrast, this shadow only reinforces it.

Do not:
Do not use it on an element pinned to a viewport edge with content scrolling under it — that is elevation.edge.<that edge>. A panel that floats over other content is elevation.floating.

floating.$description:
The lift of a container that floats over the content it belongs to. Fixed across brands and viewports; only its colour moves, with the theme.

Used in:
Dropdown panel, menu, popover, tooltip, date picker, toast — anything on color-surface.static.primary that floats over other content, including when it opens inside a modal. Always pair it with color-border.static.secondary.

Do not:
Do not use it on the surface of a scrimmed container — a modal, dialog, drawer or bottom sheet needs no shadow, its scrim (color-surface.static.overlay) does the separating, and its surface is color-surface.static.primary. Resting cards are elevation.raised.

top.$description:
The shadow of a surface anchored to the top edge, cast downward onto the content scrolling under it. Fixed across brands and viewports; only its colour moves, with the theme.

Used in:
Sticky header, top app bar, and the overflow indicator at the top of a scrolled region. Its surface is the element's own, usually color-surface.static.primary.

Do not:
Do not use it on an element that floats free of any edge — that is elevation.floating. An element anchored to the bottom edge is elevation.edge.bottom; the four are not interchangeable, the offset points the other way.

bottom.$description:
The shadow of a surface anchored to the bottom edge, cast upward onto the content scrolling under it. Fixed across brands and viewports; only its colour moves, with the theme.

Used in:
Sticky bottom bar, bottom sheet, and the overflow indicator at the bottom of a scrolled region. Its surface is the element's own, usually color-surface.static.primary.

Do not:
Do not use it on an element that floats free of any edge — that is elevation.floating. An element anchored to the top edge is elevation.edge.top; the four are not interchangeable, the offset points the other way.

left.$description:
The shadow of a surface anchored to the left edge, cast to the right onto the content scrolling under it. Fixed across brands and viewports; only its colour moves, with the theme.

Used in:
A panel or drawer docked to the left edge of the viewport or of its container. Its surface is the element's own, usually color-surface.static.primary.

Do not:
Do not use it on an element that floats free of any edge — that is elevation.floating. An element anchored to the right edge is elevation.edge.right; the four are not interchangeable, the offset points the other way.

right.$description:
The shadow of a surface anchored to the right edge, cast to the left onto the content scrolling under it. Fixed across brands and viewports; only its colour moves, with the theme.

Used in:
A panel or drawer docked to the right edge of the viewport or of its container. Its surface is the element's own, usually color-surface.static.primary.

Do not:
Do not use it on an element that floats free of any edge — that is elevation.floating. An element anchored to the left edge is elevation.edge.left; the four are not interchangeable, the offset points the other way.
